title: Prober-driven batch annealer: continuous workload profiling and safe apply/rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We need an automated recommendation engine that continuously profiles request workloads and safely applies batching and caching parameter changes to reduce per-token cost without violating latency SLOs. This ticket implements a prober-driven 'annealer' that (1) collects lightweight workload fingerprints, (2) scores candidate configurations using deterministic heuristics + offline microbench profiles, (3) runs staged canary applies with safety gates, and (4) supports automatic rollback and audit logging.

Scope: lightweight profiler (route-level), offline microbench lookup table for kernel/quant combos, heuristic scorer that outputs batch_size, max_queue_ms, prefix-KV caching policy and warmup window, an annealing controller that increments/decrements batch parameters over N windows, and a safe apply subsystem that performs canary, metrics monitoring, and automated rollback if thresholds are breached. Integrations: Redwood Console dashboards, runtime metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, cost/token), tracing and request-sampling, and rollout feature flagging.

Non-goals: model architecture changes, experiment-driven model quality adjustments, or user-facing SDK changes (those will be follow-ups).

Implementation highlights: a) Workload profiler uses economized histograms per route: sequence_length_distribution, arrival_isometry (inter-arrival percentiles), KV hit ratio estimates computed from prefix reuse heuristics. b) Candidate generator queries an offline microbenchmark DB keyed by model-variant + seq_len + hw_type to get expected tokens/sec and latency curves. c) Heuristic scorer ranks candidates by expected cost reduction subject to a latency penalty budget; scoring factors include tail latency growth estimate, queue depth, GPU utilization headroom, and KV hit sensitivity. d) Annealer executes gradual parameter changes (e.g., increase batch_size by 10% every window up to recommended target) to allow gradual kernel warming and reduce transient regressions. e) Safe apply: canary on 1-5% traffic for X minutes, evaluate SLO metrics vs baseline, automatic rollback if p99 increases > 15% absolute or error rate increases > 0.5% or cost regresses negatively for correctness thresholds. f) Operational: each apply creates an immutable rollout record with previous config, metric snapshots, and links to the prober profile used.

Why this is different: Existing autotuners select a single batch target or offline profile. The prober-driven annealer emphasizes continuous small steps, runtime-aware kernel warming, and safety-first rollouts to be usable in production-active fleets with mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler ships that collects per-route sequence-length histograms, inter-arrival percentiles, and approximate KV reuse counts with <2% additional tail latency overhead
Offline microbench DB accessible by scorer for model-variant + seq_len + hw_type lookup
Heuristic scorer returns ranked candidate configs (batch_size, max_queue_ms, kv_policy, warmup_windows) and an expected cost delta estimate
Annealer controller can apply incremental changes across configurable windows and record intermediate metric snapshots
Safe apply implementation performs canary on configurable traffic fraction, evaluates SLO gates (p99 latency, error rate, cost), and automatically rolls back on breaches
Rollout records are persisted with links to prober snapshot, scored candidates, and the prior config for audit
Console dashboard updated with per-rollout comparison charts (baseline vs candidate) and a list of recent automated rollbacks
End-to-end integration tests and a small-scale canary run executed in staging with a synthetic multi-route workload demonstrating stable p99 and >10% cost improvement on at least one route
steps: Design: finalize profiling schema and scoring heuristics (owner: Maya)
Infra: add lightweight histogram storage and retention policy (owner: Infra)
Microbenching: export model-variant lookup table for seq_len buckets (owner: Bench)
Service: implement heuristic scorer API and candidate generator (owner: Liam)
Controller: build annealer with windowing and feature-flagged applies (owner: Runtime)
Safety: implement canary gating, thresholds, and rollback logic (owner: SRE)
Console: add rollout record view and comparison charts (owner: Console UX)
Testing: unit/integration tests + staging canary + failure-injection tests (owner: QA)
Rollout: staged internal rollout to dedicated capacity customers, monitor first 2 weeks (owner: PM)
Postmortem: capture learnings and update heuristics based on observed regressions (owner: Research)
Documentation: publish runbook and ops guide for manual override and emergency rollback procedures
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching yields better unit costs but increases risk to tail latency; annealing trades rapid wins for safer stability.
Rollback policy: immediate rollback if p99 latency increases >15% absolute or error rate delta >0.5% relative to baseline during canary period.
Observability: add request sampling of 1 in 1000 for full payload capture during canary to help debug regressions.
Metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, queue length distribution, tokens/sec/GPU, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, 4xx/5xx error rates
Plan B: if automatic rollback flaps, fall back to safe preset profiles and open incident to on-call runtime eng
